title: حِكَايَةُ قَمَرِ الزَّمَانِ
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 901–903 (Night 217, continuing nights-216), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 217 continues the tale of Qamar al-Zamān. Budūr agrees that he should marry Ḥayāt al-Nufūs, and King Armānūs tells his court the whole story; the courtiers, who had served Budūr as their sultan, accept Qamar al-Zamān in her place. The marriage is contracted, the festivities held, and Qamar al-Zamān rules justly, abolishing the tolls and emptying the prisons, spending a night with each wife in turn. He forgets his father Shahramān. Each wife bears him a son: al-Amjad to Budūr, al-Asʿad to Ḥayāt al-Nufūs. The two princes grow up inseparable, accomplished and beautiful, and take turns judging in their father's place; but each queen falls in love with the other's son, and when they can find no way to him they stop eating and sleeping. The king rides out to hunt, leaving the two sons to judge; and morning overtakes Shahrazād. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ السَّابِعَةَ عَشَرَ بَعْدَ الْمِائَتَيْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-sābiʿata ʿashara baʿda al-miʾatayni
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the seventeenth after the two-hundred,
sentences.i: And when it was the two hundred and seventeenth night,
sentences.n: al-sābiʿata ʿashara, “seventeenth”: as in the nights before, the print has the masculine عشر where Classical Arabic would make it feminine (ʿashrata) to agree with the night; it is vocalised as printed. The ئ of المائتين is printed.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُأَنَّ قَمَرَ الزَّمَانِ اتَّفَقَ مَعَ زَوْجَتِهِ الْمَلِكَةِ بُدُورَ عَلَى هٰذَا الْأَمْرِ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna Qamara al-Zamāni ittafaqa maʿa zawjatihi al-malikati Budūra ʿalā hādhā al-amri
sentences.l: She-said: It-has-reached-me, O fortunate king, that Qamar al-Zamān agreed with his-wife the-queen Budūr on this matter,
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that Qamar al-Zamān came to an agreement with his wife Queen Budūr on this matter,
sentences.n: The print runs al-saʿīdu and anna together as السعيدان, as it often does in this formula; it is kept so. “This matter” is the proposal of the night before: that he should take Ḥayāt al-Nufūs, King Armānūs's daughter, as a second wife. ittafaqa maʿa … ʿalā, “to agree with (someone) on (something)”: maʿa marks the partner, ʿalā the matter.

sentences.t: وَأَخْبَرَ الْمَلِكَ أَرْمَانُوسَ بِمَا قَالَتْهُ الْمَلِكَةُ بُدُورُ مِنْ أَنَّهَا تُحِبُّ ذٰلِكَ وَتَكُونُ جَارِيَةً لِحَيَاةِ النُّفُوسِ
sentences.tr: wa-akhbara al-malika Armānūsa bi-mā qālathu al-malikatu Budūru min annahā tuḥibbu dhālika wa-takūnu jāriyatan li-Ḥayāti al-Nufūsi
sentences.l: and-he-informed the-king Armānūs of-what said-it the-queen Budūr: (namely) that-she would-love that, and-would-be a-handmaid to-Ḥayāt al-Nufūs.
sentences.i: and he told King Armānūs what Queen Budūr had said: that she would welcome it, and would be a handmaid to Ḥayāt al-Nufūs.
sentences.n: akhbara, Form IV, “to inform”, takes the person as object and bi- for what is told. qālathu: the -hu, “it”, picks up mā, “what”. min annahā …: min explains what she said, “namely that she …”. tuḥibbu dhālika, “she loves that”, here “she is glad of it”; the shadda of تحبّ is printed. jāriya, a slave-girl or handmaid: Budūr's courtesy, putting herself beneath the new wife; li- marks the one served.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْمَلِكُ أَرْمَانُوسُ هٰذَا الْكَلَامَ مِنْ قَمَرِ الزَّمَانِ فَرِحَ فَرَحًا شَدِيدًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-maliku Armānūsu hādhā al-kalāma min Qamari al-Zamāni fariḥa faraḥan shadīdan
sentences.l: And-when heard the-king Armānūs this speech from Qamar al-Zamān, he-rejoiced a-rejoicing intense.
sentences.i: When King Armānūs heard this from Qamar al-Zamān, he rejoiced greatly.
sentences.n: fariḥa faraḥan shadīdan, “he rejoiced a great rejoicing”: the verb with its own verbal noun as object, the usual way to intensify.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ خَرَجَ وَجَلَسَ عَلَى كُرْسِيِّ مَمْلَكَتِهِ وَأَحْضَرَ جَمِيعَ الْوُزَرَاءِ وَالْأُمَرَاءِ وَالْحُجَّابِ وَأَرْبَابِ الدَّوْلَةِ
sentences.tr: thumma kharaja wa-jalasa ʿalā kursiyyi mamlakatihi wa-aḥḍara jamīʿa al-wuzarāʾi wa-al-umarāʾi wa-al-ḥujjābi wa-arbābi al-dawlati
sentences.l: Then he-went-out and-sat on (the) chair (of) his-kingdom, and-had-brought all the-viziers and-the-emirs and-the-chamberlains and-the-lords (of) the-state,
sentences.i: Then he went out and sat on the throne of his kingdom, and summoned all the viziers, emirs, chamberlains and great officers of state,
sentences.n: kursī mamlakatihi, “the chair of his kingdom”, his throne. arbāb al-dawla, “the lords of the state”, the high officers. The shaddas of كرسيّ and الحجّاب are printed.

sentences.t: وَأَخْبَرَهُمْ بِقِصَّةِ قَمَرِ الزَّمَانِ وَزَوْجَتِهِ الْمَلِكَةِ بُدُورَ مِنَ الْأَوَّلِ إِلَى الْآخِرِ وَأَنَّهُ يُرِيدُ أَنْ يُزَوِّجَ ابْنَتَهُ حَيَاةَ النُّفُوسِ لِقَمَرِ الزَّمَانِ وَيَجْعَلَهُ سُلْطَانًا عَلَيْهِمْ عِوَضًا عَنْ زَوْجَتِهِ الْمَلِكَةِ بُدُورَ
sentences.tr: wa-akhbarahum bi-qiṣṣati Qamari al-Zamāni wa-zawjatihi al-malikati Budūra mina al-awwali ilā al-ākhiri wa-annahu yurīdu an yuzawwija ibnatahu Ḥayāta al-Nufūsi li-Qamari al-Zamāni wa-yajʿalahu sulṭānan ʿalayhim ʿiwaḍan ʿan zawjatihi al-malikati Budūra
sentences.l: and-he-told-them of-(the)-story (of) Qamar al-Zamān and-his-wife the-queen Budūr from the-first to the-last, and-that-he wants to give-in-marriage his-daughter Ḥayāt al-Nufūs to-Qamar al-Zamān, and-make-him sultan over-them in-place of his-wife the-queen Budūr.
sentences.i: He told them the story of Qamar al-Zamān and his wife Queen Budūr from first to last, and that he wished to marry his daughter Ḥayāt al-Nufūs to Qamar al-Zamān and make him sultan over them in place of his wife Queen Budūr.
sentences.n: bi-qiṣṣati: after akhbara, bi- marks what is told, as in the sentence before. The ā of الآخر is printed. wa-annahu yurīdu …, “and that he wants …”, is a second thing told, still governed by akhbarahum. zawwaja, Form II, “to give in marriage”: the bride is the object and li- marks the groom; the shadda of يزوّج is printed. jaʿala takes two objects, “to make (him) sultan”. ʿiwaḍan ʿan, “as a replacement for, in place of”.

sentences.t: فَقَالُوا جَمِيعًا حَيْثُ كَانَ قَمَرُ الزَّمَانِ هُوَ زَوْجَ الْمَلِكَةِ بُدُورَ الَّتِي كَانَتْ سُلْطَانًا عَلَيْنَا قَبْلَهُ وَنَحْنُ نَظُنُّ أَنَّهَا صِهْرُ مَلِكِنَا أَرْمَانُوسَ فَكُلُّنَا نَرْضَاهُ سُلْطَانًا عَلَيْنَا وَ نَكُونُ لَهُ خَدَمًا وَلَانَخْرُجُ عَنْ طَاعَتِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālū jamīʿan ḥaythu kāna Qamaru al-Zamāni huwa zawja al-malikati Budūra allatī kānat sulṭānan ʿalaynā qablahu wa-naḥnu naẓunnu annahā ṣihru malikinā Armānūsa fa-kullunā narḍāhu sulṭānan ʿalaynā wa-nakūnu lahu khadaman wa-lā nakhruju ʿan ṭāʿatihi
sentences.l: And-they-said all-together: Since Qamar al-Zamān was he the-husband (of) the-queen Budūr, who was sultan over-us before-him while-we were-thinking that-she (was the) son-in-law (of) our-king Armānūs, so all-of-us accept-him (as) sultan over-us, and we-shall-be to-him servants, and-we-shall-not-go-out from his-obedience.
sentences.i: They answered with one voice: “Since Qamar al-Zamān is the husband of Queen Budūr, who was sultan over us before him while we took her for the son-in-law of our King Armānūs, we all accept him as our sultan; we shall be his servants and never stray from obedience to him.”
sentences.n: The print has نرضاة, a misprint for نرضاه, corrected here. ḥaythu, “where”, is used in the later language for “since, seeing that”. huwa zawja: huwa is the pronoun that separates subject from predicate, and the predicate of kāna stays accusative, zawja. sulṭānan: Budūr, disguised as a man, reigned as sultan, and the word keeps its masculine form. wa-naḥnu naẓunnu, “while we were thinking”: an imperfect clause of circumstance, set in the past by the verbs around it. The feminine annahā is what the courtiers know now, not what they thought then. ṣihr, “son-in-law”. The shadda of فكلّنا is printed. narḍāhu sulṭānan, “we accept him as sultan”, with two objects. The print sets wa-, “and”, alone at the end of a line, apart from nakūnu, as it often does; and it runs wa-lā nakhruju together as ولانخرج; both are kept. kharaja ʿan ṭāʿatihi, “to go out from his obedience”, means to rebel.

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَ الْمَلِكُ أَرْمَانُوسُ بِذٰلِكَ فَرَحًا شَدِيدًا
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥa al-maliku Armānūsu bi-dhālika faraḥan shadīdan
sentences.l: And-rejoiced the-king Armānūs at-that a-rejoicing intense.
sentences.i: King Armānūs rejoiced greatly at this.
sentences.n: fariḥa bi-, “to rejoice at”: bi- marks the cause of the joy.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَحْضَرَ الْقُضَاةَ وَالشُّهُودَ وَرُؤَسَاءَ الدَّوْلَةِ وَعَقَدَ عَقْدَ قَمَرِ الزَّمَانِ عَلَى ابْنَتِهِ الْمَلِكَةِ حَيَاةِ النُّفُوسِ
sentences.tr: thumma aḥḍara al-quḍāta wa-al-shuhūda wa-ruʾasāʾa al-dawlati wa-ʿaqada ʿaqda Qamari al-Zamāni ʿalā ibnatihi al-malikati Ḥayāti al-Nufūsi
sentences.l: Then he-had-brought the-judges and-the-witnesses and-(the)-heads (of) the-state, and-he-tied (the) contract (of) Qamar al-Zamān upon his-daughter the-queen Ḥayāt al-Nufūs.
sentences.i: Then he summoned the judges, the witnesses and the heads of state, and had the marriage contract drawn up between Qamar al-Zamān and his daughter, Queen Ḥayāt al-Nufūs.
sentences.n: ʿaqada ʿaqda X ʿalā Y, “to tie the contract of X upon Y”, the phrase for concluding a marriage: the groom is named in the iḍāfa, and ʿalā marks the bride. The judges (quḍāt) and witnesses (shuhūd) are those a Muslim marriage contract requires. The ؤ and ء of رؤساء are printed.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ أَقَامَ الْأَفْرَاحَ وَأَوْلَمَ الْوَلَائِمَ الْفَاخِرَةَ وَخَلَعَ الْخِلَعَ السَّنِيَّةَ عَلَى جَمِيعِ الْأُمَرَاءِ وَرُؤَسَاءِ الْعَسَاكِرِ وَتَصَدَّقَ عَلَى الْفُقَرَاءِ وَالْمَسَاكِينِ وَأَطْلَقَ جَمِيعَ الْمَحَابِيسِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu aqāma al-afrāḥa wa-awlama al-walāʾima al-fākhirata wa-khalaʿa al-khilaʿa al-saniyyata ʿalā jamīʿi al-umarāʾi wa-ruʾasāʾi al-ʿasākiri wa-taṣaddaqa ʿalā al-fuqarāʾi wa-al-masākīni wa-aṭlaqa jamīʿa al-maḥābīsi
sentences.l: Then he set-up the-rejoicings, and-gave-as-feasts the-feasts the-splendid, and-took-off the-robes the-sublime upon all the-emirs and-(the)-heads (of) the-armies, and-gave-alms to the-poor and-the-needy, and-set-free all the-prisoners.
sentences.i: Then he held the wedding festivities and gave splendid banquets; he bestowed magnificent robes of honour on all the emirs and captains of the armies, gave alms to the poor and needy, and set all the prisoners free.
sentences.n: The print has الافراج, a misprint for الافراح, corrected here. aqāma al-afrāḥa, “he set up the rejoicings”, the set phrase for holding wedding festivities; afrāḥ, plural of faraḥ, “joy”, means in the later language a wedding. awlama al-walāʾima: verb and object from the same root, awlama, Form IV, “to give a feast”, and walīma, “banquet, wedding feast”; the ئ is printed. khalaʿa … ʿalā, “to take off (a robe) upon”, to bestow a robe of honour, the khilʿa, which a ruler took off and gave; ʿalā marks the ones honoured. taṣaddaqa ʿalā, Form V, “to give alms to”; its shadda is printed. The two clauses run in parallel, each a verb with an object from its own root: awlama al-walāʾima / khalaʿa al-khilaʿa.

sentences.t: وَاسْتَبْشَرَ الْعَالَمُ بِسَلْطَنَةِ الْمَلِكِ قَمَرِ الزَّمَانِ وَصَارُوا يَدْعُونَ لَهُ بِدَوَامِ الْعِزِّ وَالْإِقْبَالِ وَالسَّعَادَةِ وَالْإِجْلَالِ
sentences.tr: wa-istabshara al-ʿālamu bi-salṭanati al-maliki Qamari al-Zamāni wa-ṣārū yadʿūna lahu bi-dawāmi al-ʿizzi wa-al-iqbāli wa-al-saʿādati wa-al-ijlāli
sentences.l: And-rejoiced-at-the-tidings the-world at-(the)-sultanate (of) the-king Qamar al-Zamān, and-they-began praying for-him for-(the)-lasting (of) the-might and-the-good-fortune and-the-happiness and-the-honour.
sentences.i: All the world rejoiced at the sultanate of King Qamar al-Zamān, and they began to pray that his might and good fortune, his happiness and honour, might last.
sentences.n: istabshara bi-, Form X, “to take as good news, rejoice at”: bi- marks what is welcomed. al-ʿālam, “the world”, means everyone, and the verb after it is plural, ṣārū. ṣāra with an imperfect, “they began to …”. daʿā lahu bi-, “to pray for him for”: li- marks the one prayed for, bi- the blessing asked. The list rhymes: al-iqbāl / al-ijlāl.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ قَمَرَ الزَّمَانِ لَمَّاصَارَ سُلْطَانًا عَلَيْهِمْ أَزَالَ الْمُكُوسَ وَأَطْلَقَ مَنْ بَقِيَ فِى الْحُبُوسِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna Qamara al-Zamāni lammā ṣāra sulṭānan ʿalayhim azāla al-mukūsa wa-aṭlaqa man baqiya fī al-ḥubūsi
sentences.l: Then Qamar al-Zamān, when he-became sultan over-them, removed the-tolls, and-set-free whoever remained in the-prisons.
sentences.i: When Qamar al-Zamān became sultan over them, he abolished the tolls and set free whoever was still in the prisons.
sentences.n: The print runs lammā ṣāra together as لماصار; it is kept so. mukūs, plural of maks, the market dues and tolls that religious law did not sanction, which a just ruler is praised for abolishing. Armānūs has just freed “all the prisoners”; the story repeats the good deed for the new king. The rhyme falls on al-mukūs / al-ḥubūs.

sentences.t: وَسَارَ فِيهِمْ سِيرَةً حَمِيدَةً وَأَقَامَ مَعَ زَوْجَتِهِ عَلَى هَنَاءٍ وَسُرُورٍ وَوَفَاءٍ وَحُبُورٍ يَبِيتُ عِنْدَ كُلِّ وَاحِدَةٍ مِنْهُمَا لَيْلَةً
sentences.tr: wa-sāra fīhim sīratan ḥamīdatan wa-aqāma maʿa zawjatihi ʿalā hanāʾin wa-surūrin wa-wafāʾin wa-ḥubūrin yabītu ʿinda kulli wāḥidatin minhumā laylatan
sentences.l: And-he-went among-them a-going praiseworthy, and-he-stayed with his-wife in contentment and-gladness and-faithfulness and-delight, spending-the-night with each one of-the-two a-night.
sentences.i: He ruled among them in a praiseworthy way, and lived with his wives in contentment and gladness, in faithfulness and delight, spending one night with each of them in turn.
sentences.n: sāra fīhim sīratan, “he went among them a going”: sīra, from the same root as sāra, is a way of conduct, and the phrase means “he governed them”. maʿa zawjatihi: the print has the singular, “his wife”, where the sense seems to want the dual زوجتيه, “his two wives”, since the next words, “each one of the two of them”, show two, and the dual is printed a few lines on; but the singular may be an oversight of the author's as easily as of the compositor's, so it is kept, vocalised as printed, and the reading is doubtful. ʿalā here marks the state he lived in. The four nouns rhyme in pairs: hanāʾ / wafāʾ, surūr / ḥubūr. yabītu, “he spends the night”, a clause of circumstance without “and”; laylatan is an accusative of time.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَلْ عَلَى ذٰلِكَ مُدَّةً مِنَ الزَّمَانِ وَقَدِ انْجَلَتْ عَنْهُ الْهُمُومُ وَالْأَحْزَانُ وَنَسِيَ أَبَاهُ الْمَلِكَ شَهْرَمَانَ وَ مَاكَانَ لَهُ عِنْدَهُ مِنْ عِزٍّ وَسُلْطَانٍ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazal ʿalā dhālika muddatan mina al-zamāni wa-qadi injalat ʿanhu al-humūmu wa-al-aḥzānu wa-nasiya abāhu al-malika Shahramāna wa-mā kāna lahu ʿindahu min ʿizzin wa-sulṭānin
sentences.l: And-he-did-not-cease on that a-space of the-time, and-already had-cleared-away from-him the-cares and-the-sorrows, and-he-forgot his-father the-king Shahramān and-what was for-him with-him of might and-dominion,
sentences.i: So he continued for a time, his cares and sorrows lifted from him, and he forgot his father King Shahramān and all the honour and power he had had with him,
sentences.n: The print has اباة, a misprint for اباه, corrected here. lam yazal ʿalā dhālika, “he did not cease (being) upon that”, that is, he went on so. injalā ʿan, Form VII, “to clear away from”, as clouds from the sky; the feminine injalat agrees with the broken plural al-humūm. Shahramān is his father, the king he left behind in his own country. The print again sets wa- alone at a line end and runs mā kāna together as ماكان; both are kept. mā kāna lahu ʿindahu, “what he had had with him”: lahu, the one who had it, is Qamar al-Zamān; ʿindahu, “with him”, his father. min marks what mā consists of; the shadda of عزّ is printed. The rhyme runs al-zamān / al-aḥzān / sulṭān.

sentences.t: حَتَّى رَزَقَهُ اللّٰهُ تَعَالَى مِنْ زَوْجَتَيْهِ بِوَلَدَيْنِ ذَكَرَيْنِ مِثْلَ الْقَمَرَيْنِ النَّيِّرَيْنِ
sentences.tr: ḥattā razaqahu Allāhu taʿālā min zawjatayhi bi-waladayni dhakarayni mithla al-qamarayni al-nayyirayni
sentences.l: until provided-him God (He is exalted) from his-two-wives with-two-boys male, like the-two-moons the-two-shining.
sentences.i: until God, exalted is He, granted him by his two wives two sons, like the two shining luminaries.
sentences.n: razaqa, “to provide, grant”: here the gift is marked with bi-, where Classical Arabic usually has a second object; min marks the mothers. dhakarayni, “male”, makes the sex plain, as the stories like to. al-qamarāni, “the two moons”, is itself an old name for the pair sun and moon, as is al-nayyirāni, “the two luminaries”; the two boys are likened to that pair. The shadda of النيّرين is printed.

sentences.t: أَكْبَرُهُمَا مِنَ الْمَلِكَةِ بُدُورَ وَ كَانَ اسْمُهُ الْمَلِكَ الْأَمْجَدَ وَأَصْغَرُهُمَا مِنَ الْمَلِكَةِ حَيَاةِ النُّفُوسِ وَاسْمُهُ الْمَلِكُ الْأَسْعَدُ
sentences.tr: akbaruhumā mina al-malikati Budūra wa-kāna ismuhu al-malika al-Amjada wa-aṣgharuhumā mina al-malikati Ḥayāti al-Nufūsi wa-ismuhu al-maliku al-Asʿadu
sentences.l: The-elder-of-the-two from the-queen Budūr, and-was his-name the-king al-Amjad; and-the-younger-of-the-two from the-queen Ḥayāt al-Nufūs, and-his-name the-king al-Asʿad.
sentences.i: The elder was Queen Budūr's, and his name was King al-Amjad; the younger was Queen Ḥayāt al-Nufūs's, and his name was King al-Asʿad.
sentences.n: Two nominal sentences without a verb, “the elder of them (was) from …”. al-Amjad, “the Most Glorious”, and al-Asʿad, “the Most Fortunate”, are elatives used as names; with kāna the name is its predicate and accusative, al-malika al-Amjada, while in the second, verbless sentence it is nominative. The print sets wa- alone at the end of the line once more.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ الْأَسْعَدُ أَجْمَلَ مِنْ أَخِيهِ الْأَمْجَدِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna al-Asʿadu ajmala min akhīhi al-Amjadi
sentences.l: And-was al-Asʿad more-beautiful than his-brother al-Amjad.
sentences.i: Al-Asʿad was the more beautiful of the two.
sentences.n: ajmal min, “more beautiful than”: the elative with min of comparison.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمَا تَرَبَّيَا فِى الْعِزِّ وَالدَّلَالِ وَالْأَدَبِ وَالْكَمَالِ وَتَعَلَّمَا الْخَطَّ وَالْعِلْمَ وَالسِّيَاسَةَ وَالْفُرُوسِيَّةَ حَتَّى صَارَا فِي غَايَةِ الْكَمَالِ وَنِهَايَةِ الْحُسْنِ وَالْجَمَالِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahumā tarabbayā fī al-ʿizzi wa-al-dalāli wa-al-adabi wa-al-kamāli wa-taʿallamā al-khaṭṭa wa-al-ʿilma wa-al-siyāsata wa-al-furūsiyyata ḥattā ṣārā fī ghāyati al-kamāli wa-nihāyati al-ḥusni wa-al-jamāli
sentences.l: Then they-two were-reared in the-might and-the-pampering and-the-good-breeding and-the-perfection, and-they-two-learned the-handwriting and-the-learning and-the-statecraft and-the-horsemanship, until they-two-became in (the) utmost (of) the-perfection and-(the)-limit (of) the-goodliness and-the-beauty.
sentences.i: The two of them were brought up in honour and indulgence, in good breeding and every accomplishment; they learned penmanship and the sciences, statecraft and horsemanship, until they reached the height of perfection and the summit of beauty and grace.
sentences.n: tarabbā, Form V, “to be brought up”; taʿallama, Form V, “to learn”; both are dual, as is ṣārā, “the two became”, and the shaddas are printed, as is that of العزّ. Here the print writes فى with ى and then في with ي, side by side. al-khaṭṭ, “handwriting”, the fine penmanship a prince was taught. furūsiyya, the arts of the horseman: riding, the lance, the bow. The lists rhyme: al-dalāl / al-kamāl, and al-kamāl / al-jamāl.

sentences.t: وَافْتَتَنَ بِهِمَا النِّسَاءُ وَالرِّجَالُ
sentences.tr: wa-iftatana bihimā al-nisāʾu wa-al-rijālu
sentences.l: And-were-infatuated with-the-two-of-them the-women and-the-men.
sentences.i: Women and men alike were infatuated with them.
sentences.n: iftatana bi-, Form VIII, “to be enthralled by”: the verb chooses bi- for the one who enthralls. The verb comes first and stays singular and masculine before its plural subject, “the women and the men”, which is allowed in Classical Arabic too.

sentences.t: وَصَارَ لَهُمَا مِنَ الْعُمْرِ نَحْوُ سَبْعَةَ عَشَرَ عَامًا وَهُمَا مُتَلَازِمَانِ فَيَأْكُلَانِ سَوَاءً وَيَشْرَبَانِ سَوَاءً وَلَا يَفْتَرِقَانِ عَنْ بَعْضِهِمَا سَاعَةً مِنَ السَّاعَاتِ وَلَا وَقْتًا مِنَ الْأَوْقَاتِ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣāra lahumā mina al-ʿumri naḥwu sabʿata ʿashara ʿāman wa-humā mutalāzimāni fa-yaʾkulāni sawāʾan wa-yashrabāni sawāʾan wa-lā yaftariqāni ʿan baʿḍihimā sāʿatan mina al-sāʿāti wa-lā waqtan mina al-awqāti
sentences.l: And-there-came-to-be for-the-two-of-them of the-life about seventeen years, and-they-two (were) inseparable: so they-two-eat together and-they-two-drink together, and-not they-two-part from each-other an-hour of the-hours nor a-time of the-times.
sentences.i: When they were about seventeen years old, they were still inseparable: they ate together and drank together, and never parted from each other for a single hour or a single moment.
sentences.n: ṣāra lahumā mina al-ʿumri, “there came to be for them of age”, the usual way to give an age: li- marks whose age it is, and naḥwu, “about”, is the subject. sabʿata ʿashara ʿāman, “seventeen years”, is Classical here: with a masculine noun the unit takes the feminine form and ʿashara stays masculine (unlike the night's heading). The imperfects fa-yaʾkulāni … describe what kept happening; the hamza of فيأكلان is printed. ʿan baʿḍihimā, “from part of them”, is the later language's “from each other”. sāʿatan mina al-sāʿāti … waqtan mina al-awqāti, “an hour of the hours … a time of the times”, a rhyming way of saying “not for a moment”.

sentences.t: وَجَمِيعُ النَّاسِ تَحْسُدُهُمَا عَلَى ذٰلِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-jamīʿu al-nāsi taḥsuduhumā ʿalā dhālika
sentences.l: And-all the-people envies-the-two-of-them for that.
sentences.i: Everyone envied them for it.
sentences.n: The verb is feminine singular, taḥsuduhumā, with jamīʿ al-nās, “all the people”, treated as a collective. ḥasada ʿalā, “to envy (someone) for”: ʿalā marks what is envied.

sentences.t: وَلَمَّا بَلَغَا مَبْلَغَ الرِّجَالِ وَاتَّصَفَا بِالْكَمَالِ صَارَ أَبُوهُمَا إِذَا سَافَرَ يُجْلِسُهُمَا عَلَى التَّعَاقُبِ فِي مَجْلِسِ الْحُكْمِ فَيَحْكُمُ كُلُّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا يَوْمًا بَيْنَ النَّاسِ
sentences.tr: wa-lammā balaghā mablagha al-rijāli wa-ittaṣafā bi-al-kamāli ṣāra abūhumā idhā sāfara yujlisuhumā ʿalā al-taʿāqubi fī majlisi al-ḥukmi fa-yaḥkumu kullu wāḥidin minhumā yawman bayna al-nāsi
sentences.l: And-when they-two-reached (the) reaching-point (of) the-men and-were-described with-the-perfection, came their-father, when he-travelled, to-seat-them-two by the-turn in (the) sitting-place (of) the-judging, and-so judges each one of-the-two a-day among the-people.
sentences.i: When they reached manhood and had grown perfect in every quality, their father, whenever he went on a journey, would seat them by turns in the hall of judgement, and each of them would judge among the people for a day.
sentences.n: mablagh al-rijāl, “the point men reach”, manhood. ittaṣafa bi-, Form VIII, “to be marked by (a quality)”: bi- marks the quality; its shadda is printed. ṣāra … yujlisuhumā, “he came to seat them”, ṣāra with an imperfect for a habit. ʿalā al-taʿāqubi, “by succession”, in turn. majlis al-ḥukm, “the seat of judgement”, where the ruler heard cases.

sentences.t: وَاتَّفَقَ بِالْقَدَرِ الْمُبْرَمِ وَالْقَضَاءِ الْمُحَتَّمِ أَنَّ مَحَبَّةَ الْأَسْعَدِ الَّذِي هُوَ ابْنُ حَيَاةِ النُّفُوسِ وَقَعَتْ فِي قَلْبِ الْمَلِكَةِ بُدُورَ زَوْجَةِ أَبِيهِ وَأَنَّ مَحَبَّةَ الْأَمْجَدِ الَّذِى هُوَ ابْنُ الْمَلِكَةِ بُدُورَ وَقَعَتْ فِي قَلْبِ حَيَاةِ النُّفُوسِ زَوْجَةِ أَبِيهِ
sentences.tr: wa-ittafaqa bi-al-qadari al-mubrami wa-al-qaḍāʾi al-muḥattami anna maḥabbata al-Asʿadi alladhī huwa ibnu Ḥayāti al-Nufūsi waqaʿat fī qalbi al-malikati Budūra zawjati abīhi wa-anna maḥabbata al-Amjadi alladhī huwa ibnu al-malikati Budūra waqaʿat fī qalbi Ḥayāti al-Nufūsi zawjati abīhi
sentences.l: And-it-chanced, by-the-fate the-made-firm and-the-decree the-made-binding, that love (of) al-Asʿad, who he (is the) son (of) Ḥayāt al-Nufūs, fell in (the) heart (of) the-queen Budūr, (the) wife (of) his-father; and-that love (of) al-Amjad, who he (is the) son (of) the-queen Budūr, fell in (the) heart (of) Ḥayāt al-Nufūs, (the) wife (of) his-father.
sentences.i: Now it happened, by fixed fate and inescapable decree, that love for al-Asʿad, the son of Ḥayāt al-Nufūs, fell into the heart of Queen Budūr, his father's wife; and love for al-Amjad, the son of Queen Budūr, fell into the heart of Ḥayāt al-Nufūs, his father's wife.
sentences.n: ittafaqa anna, “it chanced that”. bi- marks the cause, “by (the working of) fate”; al-qadar al-mubram / al-qaḍāʾ al-muḥattam, “the fate made firm / the decree made binding”, is a stock rhyming pair. maḥabbatu al-Asʿadi, “the love of al-Asʿad”, means love for him: the name is the one loved, not the lover. Each queen falls in love with her co-wife's son, her stepson; the print writes الذي and then الذى, side by side.

sentences.t: فَصَارَتْ كُلُّ وَاحِدَةٍ مِنَ الْمَرْأَتَيْنِ تُلَاعِبُ ابْنَ ضَرَّتِهَا وَتُقَبِّلُهُ وَتَضُمُّهُ إِلَى صَدْرِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-ṣārat kullu wāḥidatin mina al-marʾatayni tulāʿibu ibna ḍarratihā wa-tuqabbiluhu wa-taḍummuhu ilā ṣadrihā
sentences.l: And-came each one of the-two-women to-play-with (the) son (of) her-co-wife, and-to-kiss-him and-to-press-him to her-breast;
sentences.i: Each of the two women began to play with her co-wife's son, kissing him and pressing him to her breast;
sentences.n: ḍarra, “co-wife”, from a root of harm, the rival wife. lāʿaba, Form III, “to play with, dally with”. The ء of المرأتين is printed, and the shaddas of ضرّتها and تقبّله.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا رَأَتْ ذٰلِكَ أُمُّهُ تَظُنُّ أَنَّهُ مِنَ الشَّفَقَةِ وَمَحَبَّةِ الْأُمَّهَاتِ لِأَوْلَادِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-idhā raʾat dhālika ummuhu taẓunnu annahu mina al-shafaqati wa-maḥabbati al-ummahāti li-awlādihā
sentences.l: and-when saw that his-mother, she-thinks that-it (is) of the-tenderness and-(the)-love (of) the-mothers for-her-children.
sentences.i: and when his mother saw it, she thought it came from the tenderness and love that mothers have for their children.
sentences.n: The hamza of رأت is printed. idhā with the perfect and then the imperfect taẓunnu: whenever this happened, she would think so. min here gives the source, “(comes) from tenderness”. maḥabba li-, “love for”: li- marks the one loved. li-awlādihā, “for her children”: the singular -hā refers to the mothers, as if to “each mother”, a looseness of the later language. The shaddas of امّه, تظنّ and الامّهات are printed.

sentences.t: وَتَمَكَّنَ الْعِشْقُ مِنْ قُلُوبِ الْمَرْأَتَيْنِ وَافْتَتَنَتَا بِالْوَلَدَيْنِ
sentences.tr: wa-tamakkana al-ʿishqu min qulūbi al-marʾatayni wa-iftatanatā bi-al-waladayni
sentences.l: And-took-firm-hold the-passion of (the) hearts (of) the-two-women, and-they-two-were-infatuated with-the-two-boys.
sentences.i: Passion took firm hold of the two women's hearts, and they were enthralled by the two youths.
sentences.n: tamakkana min, Form V, “to take firm hold of”: min marks what is seized; its shadda is printed. ʿishq is passionate, desiring love, not maḥabba. iftatanatā, feminine dual, with bi- of the one who enthralls.

sentences.t: فَصَارَتْ كُلُّ وَاحِدَةٍ مِنْهُمَا إِذَا دَخَلَ عَلَيْهَا ابْنُ ضَرَّتِهَا تَضُمُّهُ إِلَى صَدْرِهَا وَتَوَدُّ أَنَّهُ لَا يُفَارِقُهَا
sentences.tr: fa-ṣārat kullu wāḥidatin minhumā idhā dakhala ʿalayhā ibnu ḍarratihā taḍummuhu ilā ṣadrihā wa-tawaddu annahu lā yufāriquhā
sentences.l: And-came each one of-the-two, when entered upon-her (the) son (of) her-co-wife, to-press-him to her-breast and-to-wish that-he not leaves-her.
sentences.i: Whenever her co-wife's son came in to her, each would press him to her breast and wish he would never leave her.
sentences.n: dakhala ʿalā, “to come in upon, enter the presence of”: ʿalā marks the one visited. wadda anna, “to wish that”, here with a plain negative statement, “that he does not leave her”. The shaddas of ضرّتها and تودّ are printed.

sentences.t: وَلَمَّا طَالَ عَلَيْهِمَا الْمِطَالُ وَلَمْ تَجِدَا سَبِيلًا إِلَى الْوِصَالِ امْتَنَعَتَا مِنَ الشَّرَابِ وَالطَّعَامِ وَهَجَرَتَا لَذِيذَ الْمَنَامِ
sentences.tr: wa-lammā ṭāla ʿalayhimā al-miṭālu wa-lam tajidā sabīlan ilā al-wiṣāli imtanaʿatā mina al-sharābi wa-al-ṭaʿāmi wa-hajaratā ladhīdha al-manāmi
sentences.l: And-when grew-long upon-the-two the-putting-off, and-they-two-did-not-find a-way to the-union, they-two-refrained from the-drink and-the-food, and-they-two-forsook (the) sweet (of) the-sleep.
sentences.i: And when the waiting grew long for them, and they could find no way to union, they gave up food and drink and forsook the sweetness of sleep.
sentences.n: ṭāla ʿalā, “to grow long for”: ʿalā marks the ones who suffer it. miṭāl, the putting-off of a debt or promise, here the long delay of fulfilment. wiṣāl, “union”, the lovers' meeting: the word is frank, and means bodily union. The pairs rhyme: al-miṭāl / al-wiṣāl, al-ṭaʿām / al-manām. imtanaʿa min, Form VIII, “to refrain from”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْمَلِكَ تَوَجَّهَ إِلَى الصَّيْدِ وَالْقَنَصِ وَأَمَرَ وَلَدَيْهِ أَنْ يَجْلِسَا فِي مَوْضِعِهِ لِلْحُكْمِ كُلُّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا يَوْمًا عَلَى عَادَتِهِمَا
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-malika tawajjaha ilā al-ṣaydi wa-al-qanaṣi wa-amara waladayhi an yajlisā fī mawḍiʿihi li-al-ḥukmi kullu wāḥidin minhumā yawman ʿalā ʿādatihimā
sentences.l: Then the-king set-out to the-hunting and-the-chase, and-ordered his-two-sons that they-two-sit in his-place for-the-judging, each one of-the-two a-day, according-to their-custom.
sentences.i: Then the king went out to hunt and ride after game, and ordered his two sons to sit in his place to judge, each of them for a day, as they were used to doing.
sentences.n: al-ṣayd wa-al-qanaṣ, “hunting and the chase”, a near-synonymous pair. The shadda of توجّه is printed. amara takes the person as object and the thing commanded in an an-clause. li-al-ḥukm: li- of purpose, “for judging”. kullu wāḥidin minhumā yawman, “each of them a day”, is loosely tacked on, without a verb.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the-morning overtook Shahrazād, and-she-fell-silent from the-permitted speech.
sentences.i: And morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the speech allowed her.
sentences.n: The closing formula, as at the end of every night. The rhyme falls on al-ṣabāḥ / al-mubāḥ.
